devices_line: One app for iPhone, iPad and Mac.
video_title: Watch Undirect stop a page taking a tap
alt_phone: The Undirect app on iPhone, listing the destinations a page tried to reach
alt_mac: The Undirect app on a Mac, listing blocked destinations
demo_text: Five fictional sites misbehave on purpose, and one behaves. Open them in Safari with Undirect switched on and watch what it stops.
meta_privacy: Undirect collects nothing: no account, no analytics, no server. What stays on your device, and the one button that sends something.
p1: To catch a click being taken, the guard runs on the sites you switch it on for. It reads the shape of the page: the element under the pointer, where a link points, and which site a new window would go to. None of it is stored or sent.
p2: The rules you set, the hosts that were blocked and how many attempts were stopped. They live in Safari's extension storage, and a copy sits in a container that only Undirect and its extension can read, so the app can show the same list. A site switched on from a private window is kept only until the last private tab closes, and never copied for the app.
p3: The “Report a site” button opens a prefilled issue on Undirect's public repository at GitHub. It carries the address of the site and what the guard saw there. Nothing is sent until you submit it yourself, and you can edit it or close the tab first. Once submitted it is public, and GitHub's privacy policy applies.
p4: Undirect has no analytics, no advertising code, no crash reporting and no third-party libraries. Blocking uses Safari's own content blocking rules, so the extension never sees the traffic it stops.
p5: Undirect collects nothing from anyone, of any age. Any change to this page is published here with a new date.
meta_support: Help with Undirect: switching it on in Safari, setting rules, a site that stopped working, and how to reach the developer.
s_report: A site that gets past the guard is more useful as a report. The “Report a site” button in the extension opens a prefilled issue with the details filled in.
q1: Undirect does not appear in Safari
a1: Open the app once, then switch Undirect on in Safari's extension settings.
q2: How do I turn it on for a site?
a2: Open the site in Safari and press the Undirect button. The guard is off everywhere until you do. Press it again to turn it off for that site.
q3: A site stopped working after I set a rule
a3: Press the extension button, find the host and choose its default option. That removes the rule.
q4: I cannot change rules on iPhone or iPad
a4: The list in the app is read only there, because iOS gives an app no way to send changes to its own extension. Change rules from the extension button in Safari.
q5: A window I wanted was blocked
a5: Its host is in the list. Allow it on that site, or everywhere.
